# Overview

The rules that decide the posts are pure TypeScript. They do not import Vue, and they do not touch `window`. The Vue layer only holds state and calls the browser.

```text
app/pages/index.vue
  provideWeaver()
    useThreadWeaver()
      useWeaverDraft()      -> app/utils/weaver
      useWeaverClipboard()
      useWeaverSpeech()
      useWeaverPublish()
  sections call useWeaver()
```

`template.html` at the repository root is the original page. The Nuxt app is the product. Do not load Vue or Tailwind from a CDN.


# Page and state

`index.vue` calls `provideWeaver()` once. Every section calls `useWeaver()` and reads the fields it needs. That is why the page file is not a long list of constants.

`useThreadWeaver()` returns one reactive object. Templates can use `weaver.source` without `.value`.

A move that would pass either end returns the same state object. Copy checkmarks, speech, and an open QR are left alone in that case. Any real edit clears them.

## Components

The workbench is `PlatformPicker`, `SourceField`, `MarkerFields`, and `DraftTools`. A card is `PostMoveButtons`, `PostLengthRing`, and `PostActions`. Names are more than one word because the lint rule requires it.


# Splitting

`splitSource` trims the source. An empty box becomes one chunk, `b-0`, with empty text.

Otherwise the text is words. The budget is `limit - (16 + bridge.length)`. The 16 characters are room for a long counter. Words are added until the next word would pass the budget. A word that is already too long stays whole, even if the ring will turn red.

With **Keep line breaks** off, every line break is whitespace, so the words are joined with single spaces. With it on, the gap between lines is a newline, and a blank line stays blank. The newline counts toward the budget.

`compileThread` then polishes each chunk and attaches the marker. Polish can capitalize the first letter and append `…`. The `raw` field on a post is that polished text. `compiled` is the text plus the marker and the bridge.

The tests in `tests/thread.test.ts` import these functions directly. They do not reimplement the packer.


# Installation

You need [Bun](https://bun.sh). The repository is [github.com/thaikolja/thread-weaver](https://github.com/thaikolja/thread-weaver).

## Install and start

```bash
bun install
bun run dev
```

Open the URL Bun prints. The home page is the editor.

## Documentation site

The docs are a separate [Docus](https://docus.dev) app in `documentation/`. A GitHub Action writes the markdown from the source, then runs `nuxt generate`. The static files are written to the `/docs` folder at the root of the repository.


# Introduction

A long post is hard to read on a timeline. Thread Weaver splits that post into a sequence of shorter posts before you publish it.

## Who it is for

Use it when you already have the words and you need them to fit a character limit. The tool is a workbench, not a social network. It does not sign you in, and it does not keep a history of what you wrote.

## What stays on your machine

Splitting, markers, totals, and the download file are computed in the page. Copy uses the browser clipboard. Listen uses the browser speech API. Send opens the platform's compose page in a new tab and leaves the actual post to you.

The only remote call is the QR image. Send to Phone asks `api.qrserver.com` for a picture of the current post. Everything else stays local.

## Version

The project is version **1.0.0**. That number stays until the maintainer asks for a bump. It is not a production release yet.


# Components

Each file is one part of the screen. Interactive parts call `useWeaver()`. A card receives only the post and its index.

## `DraftTools.vue`

Shared editor. Text tools, the raw character count, and Clear.

## `MarkerFields.vue`

Shared editor. Marker, placement, and bridge update the posts as they change.

## `PlatformPicker.vue`

Button colors for the four corsets.

Shared editor. The page calls provideWeaver().

## `PostActions.vue`

The compiled post these buttons act on.

Shared editor.

## `PostCard.vue`

This card's compiled post and where it sits in the list.

Shared editor. Copy, the limit, and the list length live here.

## `PostLengthRing.vue`

Ring color and how full the circle is.

Compiled length against the active platform limit.

Green when short, red when the post is over the limit.

How much of the ring is still empty.

## `PostList.vue`

Shared editor. The list just reads the compiled posts.

## `PostMoveButtons.vue`

Which card this is, so the first and last arrows can disable themselves.

Shared editor. Move does not repack the text.

## `QrModal.vue`

Shared editor. The modal opens when a post asks for a QR.

## `ShipStation.vue`

Shared editor. Totals and the download live on it.

## `SourceField.vue`

Shared editor.

## `WeaverFooter.vue`

Offline footnote from the template. The QR action still calls a remote image service.

## `WeaverHeader.vue`

Thread Weaver masthead: kicker, wordmark, and the template tagline.

## `WeaverWorkbench.vue`

Presentational section of the workbench.


# Composables

The Vue layer that holds the editor and talks to the browser. The notes below are the comments on the exports, so this page follows the code.

## `app/composables/usePageMeta.ts`

### `usePageMeta`

Tab title and social tags for the one-page tool.

The title template is just the string itself, so the site name is not appended twice.

```ts
export function usePageMeta(): void
```

## `app/composables/useThreadWeaver.ts`

### `useThreadWeaver`

One editor for the page.

Draft edits clear copy checkmarks, stop speech, and close the QR, because segment ids get reused after a fresh pack.

```ts
export function useThreadWeaver()
```

## `app/composables/useWeaverClipboard.ts`

### `useWeaverClipboard`

Copy buttons and their checkmarks.

- Parameter `posts`: The cards as they look right now.

```ts
export function useWeaverClipboard(posts: ComputedRef<readonly CompiledPost[]>)
```

## `app/composables/useWeaverContext.ts`

### `weaverKey`

One editor for the whole page.

```ts
export const weaverKey: InjectionKey<ReturnType<typeof useThreadWeaver>> = Symbol('weaver')
```

### `provideWeaver`

Create the editor and make it available under this page.

```ts
export function provideWeaver(): void
```

### `useWeaver`

The editor from the nearest provideWeaver().

```ts
export function useWeaver(): ReturnType<typeof useThreadWeaver>
```

## `app/composables/useWeaverDraft.ts`

### `useWeaverDraft`

The editable draft.

Every control, including the bridge box, goes through `commit`, so the cards update immediately.

- Parameter `onChange`: Runs after a real edit. Use it to clear copy ticks, stop speech, and close the QR.

```ts
export function useWeaverDraft(onChange: () => void)
```

## `app/composables/useWeaverPublish.ts`

### `useWeaverPublish`

Send, phone QR, and the markdown download.

They read the cards at the moment you click.

```ts
export function useWeaverPublish(options: {
  posts: ComputedRef<readonly CompiledPost[]>
  platform: ComputedRef<PlatformId>
})
```

## `app/composables/useWeaverSpeech.ts`

### `useWeaverSpeech`

The Listen button.

One card talks at a time. Clicking it again stops it.

```ts
export function useWeaverSpeech()
```


# Splitting and compile

Packing, markers, bridges, and the text tools. The notes below are the comments on the exports, so this page follows the code.

## `app/utils/weaver/split.ts`

### `splitSource`

Cut the source into chunks that fit the platform, minus room for the counter and the bridge.

A single word longer than that budget is kept whole. Empty input is one empty chunk.

```ts
export function splitSource(source: string, limit: number, bridge: string, keepBreaks: boolean): ThreadBlock[]
```

## `app/utils/weaver/compile.ts`

### `inlineJoiner`

The gap between text and marker when they sit on one line.

A bridge is wrapped in spaces. No bridge means one space.

```ts
export function inlineJoiner(bridge: string): string
```

### `compileText`

Stick the counter onto one chunk.

A bridge shows up right away for every placement, so typing "..." updates the card without touching the source or the placement menu.

`none` skips the counter, so the bridge has nothing to sit next to.

```ts
export function compileText(
  text: string,
  format: MarkerFormat,
  placement: MarkerPlacement,
  bridge: string,
  index: number,
  total: number
): string
```

### `polishSegment`

Optional cleanup before the counter is attached.

Capitalize lifts the first letter. Finish sentences adds … when the chunk has no ending mark.

```ts
export function polishSegment(text: string, capitalize: boolean, finishSentences: boolean): string
```

### `compileThread`

Turn every chunk into a post, in the current order.

```ts
export function compileThread(state: Pick<WeaverState, 'blocks' | 'marker' | 'placement' | 'bridge'> & Partial<Pick<WeaverState, 'capitalize' | 'finishSentences'>>): CompiledPost[]
```


# State and metrics

Edits, totals, the ring, and the files you copy or send. The notes below are the comments on the exports, so this page follows the code.

## `app/utils/weaver/state.ts`

### `createWeaverState`

A fresh editor: X, parentheses, marker on its own line, no bridge.

```ts
export function createWeaverState(source: string = SAMPLE_SOURCE): WeaverState
```

### `setSource`

New source text. Manual order is dropped because we pack from scratch.

```ts
export function setSource(state: WeaverState, source: string): WeaverState
```

### `setCapitalize`

Capitalize the first letter of each post. The chunks stay where they are.

```ts
export function setCapitalize(state: WeaverState, capitalize: boolean): WeaverState
```

### `setFinishSentences`

Add … to a post that does not already end a sentence. Does not repack.

```ts
export function setFinishSentences(state: WeaverState, finishSentences: boolean): WeaverState
```

### `setKeepBreaks`

Keep line breaks in the posts and pack again. Manual order is dropped.

```ts
export function setKeepBreaks(state: WeaverState, keepBreaks: boolean): WeaverState
```

### `setPlatform`

Switch platform and use that platform's limit. The bridge stays.

```ts
export function setPlatform(state: WeaverState, platform: PlatformId): WeaverState
```

### `setBridge`

Change the bridge.

A longer or shorter bridge changes the budget, so we pack again.

The same length keeps the current order and still shows the new characters.

```ts
export function setBridge(state: WeaverState, bridge: string): WeaverState
```

### `setMarker`

Swap the counter style. The chunks stay where they are.

```ts
export function setMarker(state: WeaverState, marker: MarkerFormat): WeaverState
```

### `setPlacement`

Move the counter. Still no repack.

```ts
export function setPlacement(state: WeaverState, placement: MarkerPlacement): WeaverState
```

### `moveSegment`

Slide one chunk up or down.

Going past either end returns the same state, so nothing else resets.

```ts
export function moveSegment(state: WeaverState, index: number, delta: number): WeaverState
```

### `dropSegment`

Delete one chunk. The others keep their text. They are not glued back together.

```ts
export function dropSegment(state: WeaverState, index: number): WeaverState
```

## `app/utils/weaver/metrics.ts`

### `totalChars`

Add up the published length, markers and bridges included.

```ts
export function totalChars(posts: readonly CompiledPost[]): number
```

### `totalWords`

Count words in the source box. Markers and bridges are not words.

```ts
export function totalWords(source: string): number
```

### `readTimeMinutes`

Rough read time. At least a minute, otherwise about 200 words a minute.

```ts
export function readTimeMinutes(words: number): number
```

### `ringColor`

Color for the little ring.

Over the limit is a hard red. Under it, the hue slides from green toward red.

```ts
export function ringColor(currentLen: number, maxLimit: number): string
```

### `ringDashOffset`

How far around the ring the stroke should stop. 0 is a full circle.

```ts
export function ringDashOffset(length: number, limit: number): number
```

## `app/utils/weaver/publish.ts`

### `copyAllBody`

All posts, separated the way "Copy Entire Sequence" pastes them.

```ts
export function copyAllBody(posts: readonly CompiledPost[]): string
```

### `markdownBody`

A markdown file: a heading per post, same separators as copy-all.

```ts
export function markdownBody(posts: readonly CompiledPost[]): string
```

### `markdownFilename`

File name like `thread-x-1710000000000.md`.

```ts
export function markdownFilename(platform: PlatformId, timestamp: number): string
```

### `intentUrl`

Compose link with the post already encoded.

```ts
export function intentUrl(platform: PlatformId, compiled: string): string
```

### `qrImageUrl`

Image address for the phone QR. The image itself is still remote.

```ts
export function qrImageUrl(compiled: string): string
```

## `app/utils/weaver/speech.ts`

### `speechCommand`

Decide the next Listen click.

No speech API means do nothing. The same post already talking means stop.

Anything else means start that post at the usual rate.

```ts
export function speechCommand(
  apiAvailable: boolean,
  currentId: string | null,
  postId: string,
  text: string,
  isSpeaking: boolean
): SpeechCommand
```

### `armCopyAllReset`

Turn the "copied everything" flag on, then schedule it to turn off.

Tests pass their own timer so they don't have to wait 2.5 seconds.

```ts
export function armCopyAllReset(
  mark: (copied: boolean) => void,
  schedule: (fn: () => void, ms: number) => void
): void
```


# Types and limits

Platform caps, shared types, and the constants the editor starts from. The notes below are the comments on the exports, so this page follows the code.

## `app/utils/weaver/types.ts`

### `PLATFORM_LIMITS`

Character caps for the four platforms.

```ts
export const PLATFORM_LIMITS = {
  x: 280,
  bsky: 300,
  threads: 500,
  masto: 500
} as const
```

### `PlatformId`

Which corset is selected. The numbers live on PLATFORM_LIMITS.

```ts
export type PlatformId = keyof typeof PLATFORM_LIMITS
```

### `MarkerFormat`

How the little counter is written. `none` leaves the raw text alone.

```ts
export type MarkerFormat = 'parens' | 'brackets' | 'slash' | 'hash' | 'none'
```

### `MarkerPlacement`

Where that counter sits on the post.

```ts
export type MarkerPlacement = 'newline' | 'inline-after' | 'inline-before' | 'start'
```

### `ThreadBlock`

One chunk of text before the counter is added.

```ts
export interface ThreadBlock {
  id: string
  text: string
}
```

### `CompiledPost`

One post ready to copy, speak, or send.

```ts
export interface CompiledPost {
  id: string
  raw: string
  compiled: string
}
```

### `WeaverState`

Everything the editor is holding onto. `blocks` is the current order.

```ts
export interface WeaverState {
  source: string
  platform: PlatformId
  limit: number
  marker: MarkerFormat
  placement: MarkerPlacement
  bridge: string
  capitalize: boolean
  finishSentences: boolean
  keepBreaks: boolean
  blocks: ThreadBlock[]
}
```

### `SpeechCommand`

What the Listen button should do for this click.

```ts
export type SpeechCommand
  = | { type: 'noop' }
    | { type: 'cancel' }
    | { type: 'speak', text: string, rate: number }
```

## `app/utils/weaver/limits.ts`

### `SAMPLE_SOURCE`

The sentence in the box after a reload.

```ts
export const SAMPLE_SOURCE = 'Segment 1 of your unhinged monologue sits right here. Start typing or pasting above, and the engine partitions your thoughts along word boundaries before the platform limits humiliate you.'
```

### `COPY_ALL_RESET_MS`

How long "All Copied!" stays on screen, in milliseconds.

```ts
export const COPY_ALL_RESET_MS = 2500
```

### `SPEECH_RATE`

How fast Listen talks. 1 is normal.

```ts
export const SPEECH_RATE = 1.05
```

### `MARKER_RESERVE`

Room we leave for a counter like `(999/999)` before the bridge length is added.

```ts
export const MARKER_RESERVE = 16
```

### `platformLabel`

The name people see for the active platform.

```ts
export function platformLabel(platform: PlatformId): string
```

### `intentPrefix`

The start of the compose link for that platform.

```ts
export function intentPrefix(platform: PlatformId): string
```

## `app/utils/weaver/platformClass.ts`

### `platformButtonClass`

Classes for one platform button.

Active buttons use the brand color. The others stay quiet.

```ts
export function platformButtonClass(platform: PlatformId, active: PlatformId): string
```


# Markers and bridges

A marker is the small counter on a post. A bridge is the text you type between the post and that counter.

## Markers

<table>
<thead>
  <tr>
    <th>
      Style
    </th>
    
    <th>
      Example
    </th>
  </tr>
</thead>

<tbody>
  <tr>
    <td>
      Parentheses
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        (1/3)
      </code>
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      Brackets
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        [1/3]
      </code>
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      Raw fraction
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        1/3
      </code>
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      Number tag
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        #1
      </code>
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      None
    </td>
    
    <td>
      The post text only
    </td>
  </tr>
</tbody>
</table>

The default is parentheses. Changing the marker does not pack the text again, so an order you arranged by hand stays put. `none` does not insert a bridge, because there is no counter to attach it to.

## Placement

<table>
<thead>
  <tr>
    <th>
      Placement
    </th>
    
    <th>
      Result
    </th>
  </tr>
</thead>

<tbody>
  <tr>
    <td>
      New line (bottom)
    </td>
    
    <td>
      The marker sits under the text. A bridge gets its own paragraph.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      Header (top)
    </td>
    
    <td>
      The marker sits above the text. A bridge gets its own paragraph.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      Inline after
    </td>
    
    <td>
      The marker follows the text on the same line.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      Inline before
    </td>
    
    <td>
      The marker leads the text on the same line.
    </td>
  </tr>
</tbody>
</table>

An empty bridge is a blank line, or a single space when the marker is inline. A bridge you type shows up immediately. You do not have to edit the source or change the placement first.

Inline posts join the bridge as a space, the bridge, and a space: `${bridge}`.


# Platforms

Each platform is a character budget. Switching platform packs the source again and drops any order you arranged by hand.

<table>
<thead>
  <tr>
    <th>
      Platform
    </th>
    
    <th>
      Id
    </th>
    
    <th>
      Limit
    </th>
  </tr>
</thead>

<tbody>
  <tr>
    <td>
      X
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        x
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      280
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      Bluesky
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        bsky
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      300
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      Threads
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        threads
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      500
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      Mastodon
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        masto
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      500
    </td>
  </tr>
</tbody>
</table>

The default is X.

## What the limit means

The packer does not fill the whole limit with your words. It keeps 16 characters for a counter such as `(999/999)`, plus the length of the custom bridge. A single word that is still longer than that budget is left whole. The ring then turns red, `hsl(0, 90%, 45%)`, because the published post can exceed the limit.

Send opens one of these addresses, with the current post encoded on the end:

- `https://x.com/intent/tweet?text=`
- `https://bsky.app/intent/compose?text=`
- `https://www.threads.net/intent/post?text=`
- `https://mastodon.social/share?text=`


# Shipping a thread

The ship station is the summary under the cards.

## Totals

- **Total length** is the sum of the published posts, markers and bridges included.
- **Total words** counts words in the source box, not in the counters.
- **Read time** is at least one minute, otherwise `round(words / 200)`.
- **Format target** is the platform name, such as X or Bluesky.

## Copy

Copy on a card writes that post. Copy Entire Sequence joins every post with a blank line, `---`, and another blank line. The sequence button says it copied, then clears that label after 2.5 seconds.

Editing the draft clears those checkmarks. Segment ids are reused after a fresh pack, and a checkmark must not stick to a different sentence.

## Download

Download .md saves `thread-<platform>-<timestamp>.md`. Each post is a `### Post N` section, joined the same way as copy-all.

## Listen and QR

Listen speaks the published post at rate 1.05. Clicking the same card again stops it. Send to Phone opens a QR for that post. Closing the draft, or editing it, closes the QR as well.


# Text tools

Three switches sit under the marker fields. Each one has an icon. They replace the old "Flatten blank lines" control, which did not change the packed posts: a blank line was already treated as a space.

## Capitalize posts

The first visible letter of each post becomes uppercase. The chunks are not packed again, so the order stays. `alpha beta` is published as `Alpha beta`.

## Finish sentences

If a post does not already end with `.`, `!`, `?`, `…`, or `...`, the page adds `…`. `Hello.` is left alone. `Hello` becomes `Hello…`. The extra character is part of the published length, so the ring can move.

## Keep line breaks

Off, which is the default, a line break is just another space. `hello` and `world` on two lines become `hello world`.

On, a line break stays in the post, and a blank line stays a blank line. Turning this on packs the source again and drops a hand-made order, because the shape of the chunks can change.


# The workbench

The page is one screen. The sections share a single editor through `provideWeaver()` and `useWeaver()`. The page file itself does not hold a long list of state.

## A normal pass

1. Leave the sample sentence or replace it.
2. Pick the platform. The character ring uses that platform's limit.
3. Set the marker and, if you want one, the bridge.
4. Turn on a text tool only when you want that change.
5. Copy a card, copy the whole sequence, or download the Markdown file.

Clear empties the box. The page then shows one empty card so the marker still has a place to sit.


# Thread Weaver

Thread Weaver is a one-page editor. You paste a long post. The page cuts it into shorter posts that stay on word boundaries and fit the platform you picked.

The work happens in the browser. The page does not store the text and it does not post for you.
